gen-dafont-brusher-fs-asap: Brusher's calligraphic strokes swell like cord, every curve as heavy as its stems. Asap stands up tall beside it in sans-serif form, readable and crisp, a lowercase nearly as high as its capitals.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-epilogue: Loose, romantic brushwork up top. Epilogue follows in a tall-bodied sans with stubby ascender tips, wire-thin and curvy, so the script gets room to move while the text stays easygoing.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-fira-sans: A wide-open e never looks squeezed in Brusher's cord-like script. Fira Sans offers the opposite temperament, a plain sans with a large x-height and no thick-thin contrast, which gives the dynamic heading something sturdy to lean on.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-public-sans: Public Sans reads hefty and trustworthy, with broad openings in its c and s. Brusher's pen line holds one width throughout, a romantic script that sits next to that sturdy sans-serif body like handwriting beside print.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-supreme: Romantic and loose, Brusher flows in heavy cord-like curves. Supreme sets a crisp, dense sans strip beneath it, letters held open rather than curled shut, so the script's motion has firm footing.
gen-dafont-brusher-general-sans: Brusher hits with brushy, romantic energy, its curves thick as cord. And General Sans carries a longer stretch of text smoothly, a plain sans with steady pen pressure and an x-height that fills each line.
gen-dafont-brusher-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, with a clear gap at every curve's mouth and barely any step down from capitals. Brusher's script adds the swagger.
gen-dafont-brusher-montserrat: Geometric and approachable, Montserrat gives each curve generous white space, with oversized e and a counters in a plain sans line. Longer text glides along like wire.
gen-dafont-brusher-satoshi: Satoshi is a sans-serif with a soaring x-height and every stroke cut to one width, friendly and plain-spoken. Brusher is the one for dynamic calligraphic flourish; Satoshi handles the quiet work.
gen-dafont-brusher-switzer: Brusher is a calligraphic hand whose curves are as heavy as its stems, like cord. And Switzer, a sans-serif with tubular, wire-like letterforms and a tall waist line, brings a Swiss tidiness that keeps the romance in check.
